findings.title: Confusing logic in enableSqlExpressions that always returns false
findings.body: The new `enableSqlExpressions` function uses unnecessarily complex logic to always return false. The variable `enabled` is assigned `!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, meaning `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF — the opposite of what the name suggests. Both branches then return `false`, so the feature flag value is completely ignored. This is confusing and error-prone: a future maintainer may attempt to 'fix' what looks like an inverted boolean bug and inadvertently re-enable SQL Expressions, reintroducing CVE-2024-9264. A safer implementation would simply be `return false` with a comment explaining that SQL Expressions are permanently disabled due to CVE-2024-9264, making the intent unambiguous and removing any appearance that the feature flag is consulted.

findings.title: Dead reference to FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` queries `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions` but the result is never used — both code paths return `false`. Either the feature toggle and its documentation should be removed (since SQL Expressions are now hard-disabled regardless of the flag), or the function should be simplified to make clear the flag is intentionally ignored. Leaving a feature toggle that appears to gate behavior but actually does nothing is misleading for operators and future developers.

findings.title: No tests verifying SQL Expressions are disabled
findings.body: This is a security fix (CVE-2024-9264) that hard-disables SQL Expressions, but no tests are added to `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` (or any new test file) to verify that a `QueryTypeSQL` query now returns the expected 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error. Without a regression test, a future change could re-enable the SQL code path silently. At minimum, a test that constructs an `ExpressionQueryReader`, calls `ReadQuery` with a `QueryTypeSQL` JSON payload, and asserts the returned error would lock in the security fix.

findings.title: SQL command construction path still reachable if reader check is removed
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` still calls `sql.TablesList` which constructs a DuckDB command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)`. Currently this is unreachable because `reader.go` rejects `QueryTypeSQL` upfront, but the code path remains live and `TablesList` is still an exported function in `pkg/expr/sql`. If the `enableSqlExpressions` gate in `reader.go` is later weakened or removed (e.g., because someone misreads the confusing boolean logic in `enableSqlExpressions`), the original DuckDB-based command construction — including the string interpolation that contributed to CVE-2024-9264 — would be reachable again. Consider making `TablesList` and `NewSQLCommand` return an 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error directly rather than relying solely on the reader-level gate, so the vulnerable code path cannot be reached even if the reader check is bypassed.
